In his days, Israel and Judah will be saved and dwell on him. Isaiah says: Behold, the virgin will have in her womb and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel, which is translated 'God with us'. pass_b_english: We ask that God have mercy on us and dwell among humans, so that all people can see His salvation.
As Solomon said, if God truly dwells with humans.
This is the God who became human, as Jeremiah proclaimed, and there is no other like Him.
He gave knowledge to Jacob and Israel, and David declared that truth arose from the earth, and a man was born, founded by God Himself.
The prophets also spoke of God's presence among humans, with Hosea saying that his flesh is from them, and Isaiah stating that God is with us, and that He was found by those who did not seek Him.
In Him, people will pray, because He is the one true God, and David affirmed that the Lord's offspring will remain forever, and that God swore to David and will not revoke His promise.

The Lord will set His offspring on the throne, and their throne will endure like the heavens, as Isaiah also said: 'I will put his kingdom on David's throne to establish and take hold in righteousness and judgment.' (Isaiah 9:6-7)

As Jeremiah prophesied, the days are coming when God will raise up a righteous branch for David, and he will reign as king, demonstrating his understanding and wisdom in judgment and righteousness on the earth. (Jeremiah 23:5-6)
During his reign, Israel and Judah will be saved and will dwell in safety.
The prophet Isaiah also foretold the birth of Christ, saying that a virgin would conceive and bear a son, and his name would be called Emmanuel, which means 'God with us'. (Isaiah 7:14)

Furthermore, Ezekiel described a vision in which the Lord said to him, 'Son of man, this gate will be closed, and no one will pass through it, except the Lord God alone, who will enter and sit, and then go out and close the doors behind him, and the gate will remain closed forever.' (Ezekiel 44:1-3)
In a similar vein, Job lamented, 'Why did you not close the doors of my mother's womb for me?' (Job 3:10)
Meanwhile, Isaiah proclaimed, 'Before the one in labor gives birth, before the pains of labor come, she has escaped and given birth to a male.' (Isaiah 66:7)

The anointing of Christ is also a significant theme, as David said, 'Therefore, God anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions,' (Psalm 45:7) and Isaiah declared, 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me.' (Isaiah 61:1)
Finally, Jeremiah expressed his sorrow, saying, 'Woe is me, mother.' (Jeremiah 4:31; 15:20)
David cried out to God, 'My God, my God, attend to me.' (Psalm 22:1)
For it is God who drew me out of my mother's womb and placed me in the care of my parents.
From the moment of my birth, I was cast upon God, and he has been my rock and my salvation.
The prophet Daniel saw a vision of a stone cut without hands, which would strike the image of worldly power and bring about a new era of peace and righteousness. (Daniel 2:34-35)
The stone, as Isaiah foretold, would be a stone of stumbling in Zion, a rock of offense to those who refuse to believe. (Isaiah 8:14)
Yet, for those who put their faith in God, this stone would be a source of strength and comfort.
Zechariah saw a vision of this stone, with seven eyes looking out upon all the earth. (Zechariah 3:9; 4:10)
The birth of Jesus, as foretold by Isaiah, would be a moment of great joy and celebration, for a child is born to us, a son is given to us, and his government would be upon his shoulder. (Isaiah 9:6)
The magi, as David prophesied, would come to worship him, bringing gifts.
